claim: First quantitative lower bounds for 4-color grid Ramsey minima (ROADMAP D-3, session 2026-11-15): T_4(41,5) >= 1, T_4(31,6) >= 2, T_4(29,7) >= 3, T_4(23,10) >= 4, T_4(25,9) >= 6 (all proven CP-SAT optima of the joint two-sided aggregation relaxation, hence valid LBs on T_4; every real coloring induces a feasible point). All orientation-symmetric. Prior art (Rule 0 checks 2026-11-11 F-24 audit and 2026-11-15 web search): FGGP arXiv:1005.3750 gives EXISTENCE-only information for c=4 (OBS_4 = {G_41,5, G_31,6, G_29,7, G_25,9, G_23,10, G_22,11, G_21,13, G_19,17} + transposes, Thm 7.7); no minimum-count values for c>=3 exist anywhere in the literature, let alone c=4. These five LBs are the first counts at c=4.
tool: tools/joint_relax.py (joint two-sided aggregation relaxation, F-27 build, used unmodified, --colors 4)
environment: ortools CP-SAT 9.9.3963, 4 workers, 180 s solve limit per size
discriminators: Self-checks at FGGP-proven 4-COLORABLE grids all return OPTIMAL 0 as required: 18x18 (Thm 7.6), 21x12 (Thm 7.4), 22x10 (Thm 7.5). Blind spots: 19x17/17x19 proven-OPTIMAL 0 despite FGGP Thm 7.2 non-4-colorability (honest negative; the relaxation cannot see this instance, as at c=3 11x10). Timeouts: 22x11/11x22 FEASIBLE bound 0 at 180 s — no claim.
fggp_boundary_note: G_17,17 IS 4-colorable (the solved $289 challenge, Steinbach-Posthoff 2012, per the FGGP full text) so T_4(17,17) = 0; the Gasarch-blog-comment claim that 4 monochromatic rectangles are a hard-limit minimum for 17x17 4-colorings is refuted by that coloring's existence.
